title: Bean stem maggot (Bean fly) in common bean

Header: Bean stem maggot (Bean fly) in common bean
Ophiomyia spp. Nzi wa Maharage in Swahili

Prevention: Plant 1-2 weeks earlier in cropping season to escape heavy infestation of bean flies.
Ootheca beetle infestations, a 1-2 week delay is advised.

N + 5 t farm manure per ha, but this depends on soil conditions)
Frequently irrigate to reduce water stress and strengthen plant to better tolerate bean flies.

Crop rotation can reduce fly populations, e.g. rotate with sweet potato in short rain season.
Monitoring: Look for yellowing and stunting of plants at 2-3 leaf stage.
Then search for thickening of the stem at soil level.
This thickening is made by the fly larvae feeding inside.
Larvae hollow out stems and cannot be reached by chemical sprays.
If first damage is seen, then regularly scout for 2 mm small blackish bean flies on bean leaves from plant emergence up to 2- leaf-stage of plants.
Search for oviposition punctures on leaves caused by bean flies.
At 3-4 adult bean flies on plants/squaremeter consider direct control.
Direct Control: Earth up soil around the plant stem to cover damaged part so as to encourage root growth.
Apply neem leaf extract solutions mixed with soap max 3 times; (2.5-3 litres/ha or 50-60 ml /20 litres water, or 20 – 50 g neem seed cake or seed powder/ litre water).
Remove and destroy crop residues after harvest to kill the larvae and pupae of bean flies which live and remain in the bean stems.
Seeds coated with imidacloprid (Gaucho, and others) , or with diazinon (2 ml per kg seed)
